data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
learningPoints: Practises present continuous for actions happening now.
Builds contrast between present simple and present continuous.
ESOL B1 and aligns with IELTS 4.5–5.5 and TOEFL iBT 42–71 score ranges.

sections.explain: 'Will' + base verb makes a prediction: 'will travel'. It never takes '-s' or 'to'.

words.word: One day, people will travel to Mars.
One day, people will to travel to Mars.
One day, people will travels to Mars.

sections.summary: Use 'will' for decisions made at the moment.
sections.explain: 'Will' is used when we decide something now.

words.word: I'm tired. I will take a taxi.
I'm tired. I am going to take a taxi every day.
I'm tired. I taking a taxi.

sections.explain: 'Will' is often used to make promises.

words.word: I will help you with your homework.
I am going to helped you with your homework.
I will helping you with your homework.

sections.explain: Use 'will' + base verb for a promise: 'will call'. '-ing' and 'to' are not used after 'will'.

words.word: Don't worry, I will to call you tonight.
Don't worry, I will call you tonight.
Don't worry, I will calling you tonight.

sections.explain: 'Will' can express predictions about the future.

words.word: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
I think it is going be sunny tomorrow.
I think it going to sunny tomorrow.

sections.explain: The negative of 'will' is 'won't' + base verb: 'won't be'. 'willn't' is not a word, and no 'to' follows.

words.word: She won't to be at the office tomorrow.
She willn't be at the office tomorrow.
She won't be at the office tomorrow.

sections.explain: Future questions with 'will' invert subject and auxiliary.

words.word: Will you visit the museum tomorrow?
Do you will visit the museum tomorrow?
Will you visiting the museum tomorrow?

sections.explain: Questions with 'will' invert: 'Will you help...?'. The verb stays in the base form, and we don't add 'do'.

words.word: Will you helps me with this box?
Will you help me with this box?
Do you will help me with this box?

sections.explain: 'Will' is used for offers made at the moment of speaking.

words.word: I will carry your luggage.
I am going carry your luggage.
I will carrying your luggage.

sections.explain: 'Will' + base verb predicts: 'will do'. No 'to' or '-ing' after 'will'.

words.word: I'm sure you will doing well.
I'm sure you will to do well.
I'm sure you will do well.
